Ophthalmology · published research

Eyelid ptosis

One case report described resolution of bilateral botulinum-toxin-induced ptosis after ten GaAs laser sessions. The uncontrolled report cannot establish that laser caused recovery.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

One case report described resolution of bilateral botulinum-toxin-induced ptosis after ten GaAs laser sessions. The uncontrolled report cannot establish that laser caused recovery.

Summary of the Evidence

One publication in the exact eyelid-ptosis mapping is a human case report. It describes one patient and offers no comparison group. The source category provides no clinical replication, animal model, or separate laboratory study. Majlesi et al. 2008

Human and clinical evidence

The report concerns a 46-year-old woman with bilateral ptosis after botulinum toxin type A injection. Complete recovery was described after ten sessions of GaAs laser treatment, with the cosmetic result reported to persist for several months. The paper does not provide a controlled comparison or a quantitative measure that separates treatment effect from the natural course of toxin-associated ptosis. A single case cannot establish effectiveness for aponeurotic, neurologic, congenital, or other forms of ptosis.

Animal evidence

No animal study directly addressing eyelid ptosis was identified in the mapped records.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No in-vitro or ex-vivo evidence directly addressing eyelid-muscle or levator function was identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The case report used a GaAs laser and ten treatment sessions. The source does not provide enough treatment detail to define a reproducible parameter set, and the indication was a specific post-injection complication. Results cannot be generalized to other causes of ptosis or to routine treatment decisions.

Interpretation

The report is hypothesis-generating only. It documents a temporal association between a treatment course and recovery, but no comparator, independent replication, or established mechanism for clinical benefit is available. Current evidence is insufficient to estimate an effect or recommend the approach for eyelid ptosis.

Evidence strength in source summaryPtosis resolution: Single-case signal only
Publications and records1 publication: 1 human case report describing one patient.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Evidence is a single uncontrolled case report of botulinum-toxin-associated ptosis. Complete recovery followed ten laser sessions, but spontaneous recovery and other care cannot be excluded. There is no comparative study, replication, or evidence for other causes of eyelid ptosis. Case reports are highly vulnerable to natural recovery and selection.

Publication and study types

  • There is no control group and no independent replication.
  • A cohort count is not applicable beyond the single reported case.
  • No animal, in-vitro, or ex-vivo evidence is listed for this indication.

Research countries listed

  • Iran
